findings.summary: The named run commands don't reach every test the demonstration relies on.
findings.evidence: Criterion 3 runs `cargo test --locked -p athena-core urgent_reason`, but the fake-agent test for a speed-improving request versus an ordinary one is planned in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, which is in a different package. Criterion 4 runs `-p athena-cli priority`, but the set_priority validation tests sit next to Athena::set_priority in crates/athena-core/src/store.rs. Fix: Name both commands for each criterion (for example also `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain urgent`), or put the tests where the named command runs them. Give the tests names that match the filters.

findings.summary: The plan doesn't say how the hash is computed. athena-cli has no direct sha2 dependency, and adding one would change Cargo.lock under --locked.
findings.evidence: sha2 is declared only in athena-git, athena-data and xtask Cargo.toml. athena_data::sha256_hex already exists at crates/athena-data/src/lib.rs:36. Fix: Use athena_data::sha256_hex in the test instead of adding sha2 to athena-cli.

findings.summary: The pinned prefix should cover the base file exactly, trailing newline included, so that D122 is added purely by appending.
findings.evidence: The last entry is D121, at docs/decisions.md:2967. If the base file has no final newline, the append has to add one, but that still lies past the pinned length. Fix: Record the exact base length, and let the test check that the next byte after the prefix (if any) starts the new entry or is a blank line.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading files with Read/Grep; I ran nothing. The places the plan names exist. plan.rs has enum Priority and from_text, and plan.rs:644 currently asserts that 'Priority: urgent' parses to Normal, which step 2 already plans to fix. D121 is the last entry in docs/decisions.md, and D118 is the decision that introduced request priorities. decisions.rs already has a test module. Two design choices fit the request. Priority resolves in one method, JobRecords::priority(), shared by plan and status, in the order: priority record, then request text, then reading, then Normal. The urgent rule lives in the outputs.rs schema doc comment, so reader.md does not grow. Pinning a hash of the base-length prefix is a reasonable mechanical stand-in for comparing against the base commit. The demonstrations would fail without the behavior. The remaining issues are minor: some demonstrations name run commands in the wrong package, and the plan should reuse the existing athena_data::sha256_hex rather than add a dependency. Nothing blocks the plan.
